name: Asset-manage real estate, infrastructure and energy holdings with partners
summary: Real Assets owns about 200 real estate, infrastructure and energy investments, most of them run day to day by operating partners or company management. Each quarter the team reviews the partner's or company's report, re-keys the figures into its own models, sends valuation inputs to the independent valuation group, meets the partner or sits on the board, and approves business plans, budgets, major leases, capital projects and financings that need the fund's consent. A quarterly portfolio review decides whether to hold, watch or sell. Partners report in their own formats and on their own timetables, and consent requests and board dates are set by others, so most of the elapsed time is waiting.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian public pension investment manager whose Real Assets department of about 250 people holds about 200 real asset investments with about 60 operating partners.
baseline.notes: Real estate joint ventures with operating partners; infrastructure, power and energy companies with board seats; Portfolio Value Creation and Sustainable Investing sit in the department.

trigger: The operating partner's or company's quarter-end reporting package arrives, a newly closed holding is handed over, or a value creation plan is launched.
end_state: The quarterly asset note is filed with valuation inputs sent and consents decided, or a disposition proposal is sent to the disposition process.

volume.seasonality: Work bunches in the six to eight weeks after quarter end; annual business plans and budgets cluster in the last quarter of the partner's year; sustainability data is collected between April and July.

evidence.note: Process map volume of about 250 asset-quarters a quarter. Real Assets reported 179 investments in F2020 and 204 in F2021; some investments hold several separately managed assets.

Reviews partner and company reports, prepares property valuation inputs, records decisions and files the quarterly note. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Logs packages and re-keys partner data into internal models. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.

Updates infrastructure and energy cash flow models, prepares board briefing notes, analyses business plans and consents and drafts disposition proposals. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Runs quarterly partner and joint venture committee meetings and watch-list plans. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Sits on the boards of infrastructure and energy portfolio companies. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Approves consents and business plans and chairs the quarterly portfolio review. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Consolidates assets into the department's quarterly portfolio report. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Reviews value creation plans for material direct investments. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.
Reviews partners' annual sustainability data and climate updates. Estimated from hands-on time per asset-quarter times about 83 asset-quarters a month.

systems.name: Deal pipeline and relationship management system
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse
Private investments administration and cash flow system
Document management and investment committee memo repository
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging

steps.name: Log the quarterly package and route the asset
steps.description: The analyst saves the partner's or company's quarter-end package to the asset folder, logs its date against the reporting deadline in the joint venture or shareholder agreement and routes the asset as newly closed, partner-run real estate, or an infrastructure or energy company with a board seat.
inputs: partner quarterly report or company management report

next.condition: newly closed holding handed over from the closing team
real estate joint venture or platform run by an operating partner
infrastructure, power or energy company with a board seat

evidence.note: Mix from F2021 holdings: 152 real estate investments against 43 infrastructure and energy investments plus power and renewables platforms; new holdings about 5% of asset-quarters.

steps.name: Set up asset management for a newly closed holding
steps.description: The senior associate sets up the asset file: reporting deadlines and contents from the agreements, the approved business plan as the baseline, thresholds for leasing, capital and debt decisions that need the fund's consent, and the board or committee calendar.

error.defect_description: A consent threshold or reporting deadline is set up wrongly.

evidence.note: Reserved matters and business plans set in joint venture agreements; onboarding practices in the 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review the partner's quarterly report
steps.description: The associate compares net operating income, occupancy, leasing activity, capital spending, development progress and debt covenants with the approved budget and last quarter, reads the partner's commentary and lists questions.

error.defect_description: A covenant or leasing risk is missed.

evidence.note: Associates monitor investment performance and analyse budgets, leasing plans and capital plans. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Re-key partner data into the internal asset model
steps.description: The analyst copies property-level income, occupancy, leasing and capital figures from the partner's spreadsheet or PDF into the fund's asset model and portfolio database, because each partner reports in its own format.

evidence.note: 58 operating partners each reporting in their own format; re-keying effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Query the partner on missing or inconsistent data
steps.description: The associate emails the partner's asset manager with the list of gaps and inconsistencies (rent roll not matching income, missing capital spend detail, covenant calculations) and agrees when corrected data will arrive.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the partner's corrected data
steps.description: The partner's asset manager or property manager looks into the queries, corrects the schedules or explains the differences, and resends the package by email.

evidence.note: Partner response time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare property valuation inputs and send them to Valuations
steps.description: The associate updates the income forecast, leasing and capital assumptions and market evidence (recent sales, capitalisation rates), writes a short note on value drivers and sends the pack to the valuation group, which also manages the annual external appraisal.

error.defect_description: Out-of-date leasing assumption used in the forecast.

control.basis: Valuation policy and calendar: investment teams supply quarter-end valuation inputs to the independent valuation group by its deadline

evidence.note: Finance values private holdings independently each quarter; directly owned real estate is externally appraised at least every 12 months under GIPS. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Hold the quarterly partner or joint venture committee meeting
steps.description: The principal meets the operating partner, in person or by video, to review results, leasing, capital projects, financing and the outlook, and takes the fund's position on items the partner brings for approval.

next.condition: business plan, budget, major lease, capital project or financing needs the fund's consent

evidence.note: Joint venture reserved matters include business plan approval and new debt; associates join meetings with partners. Annual business plans fall in one quarter of four. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review the company's quarterly management report
steps.description: The associate reviews the quarter's monthly and quarter-end reports from the infrastructure or energy company: operating availability or production, regulatory and tariff matters, safety incidents, capital projects and debt, against budget and the investment case.

error.defect_description: A regulatory or safety issue is not flagged.

evidence.note: Principals oversee financial and operating performance of portfolio companies; monthly packs and quarterly covenant reporting are standard. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Update the long-term cash flow model and send valuation inputs
steps.description: The senior associate rolls the company's long-term cash flow model forward for actual results, the latest budget, regulatory decisions and interest rates, and sends the valuation input pack with a commentary to the valuation group.

error.defect_description: Model roll-forward error or stale discount rate input.

control.basis: Valuation policy and calendar: investment teams supply quarter-end valuation inputs to the independent valuation group by its deadline

evidence.note: Principals lead portfolio company valuation analyses. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the board pack
steps.description: Company management circulates the board pack a few days before the meeting; a few companies hold no formal meeting in the quarter.

next.condition: no formal board meeting this quarter

evidence.note: Boards meet at least four times a year; packs go out 3 to 7 days before.

steps.name: Prepare the board briefing note
steps.description: The senior associate reads the board pack, reconciles it to the model and variance notes, takes input from Portfolio Value Creation where relevant, and writes the director's briefing note with questions and recommended positions.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Attend the board meeting and vote
steps.description: The director nominated by the fund attends the board, challenges management on safety, operations, regulation and capital plans, and votes within the fund's agreed positions.

next.condition: budget, capital project, refinancing or acquisition needs the fund's position

evidence.note: Principals and above sit on portfolio company boards as members or observers; meetings run 2 to 4 hours plus reading. Infrastructure seeks meaningful governance rights (src2).

steps.name: Analyse the business plan or consent request
steps.description: The senior associate analyses the partner's or management's proposal (annual business plan and budget, a major lease, a capital or development project, new debt or an add-on acquisition), tests it against the asset model and drafts the fund's recommended position.

error.defect_description: Capital cost or leasing downside not tested.

evidence.note: Associates analyse proposed budgets, leasing plans, capital plans and development recommendations. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve the fund's consent or vote
steps.description: The group head reviews the recommendation and approves the fund's consent or vote; a request for new capital beyond the approved business plan is sent to the investment committees as a follow-on.

control.basis: Joint venture or shareholder agreement reserved matters and Investment Management Authorities: group head approval of consents; follow-on capital needs IDC or PEC approval

next.condition: needs new capital beyond the approved plan

evidence.note: Investment Management Authorities and IDC or PEC approval of follow-on transactions; shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Open a follow-on capital request in the deal pipeline
steps.description: The associate records the request (development funding, a partner's capital call above plan, an add-on acquisition) as an opportunity in the pipeline system so that it follows the diligence and committee route.

evidence.note: The process map has no link from asset management to screening or diligence for follow-ons; the author assumes a pipeline entry.

steps.name: Record decisions and actions in the asset file
steps.description: The associate writes up the meeting outcome, the fund's consents and votes and follow-up actions, and updates the asset's flags (covenants, leasing risk, capital projects, safety).

next.condition: material direct investment with a value creation plan
annual sustainability data cycle falls in this quarter

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review annual sustainability and climate data with the partner
steps.description: Once a year a Sustainable Investing specialist and the associate review the partner's or company's energy, emissions, water, safety and certification data and, where climate risk is material, the climate scenario update, and agree improvement actions.

error.defect_description: Partner data reported on a different basis from prior years.

control.basis: Policy on Sustainable Investing: monitoring of material sustainability and climate factors during ownership

evidence.note: KPI framework and climate framework applied to existing assets; real estate owners report sustainability data annually between April and July. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review value creation plan progress with Portfolio Value Creation
steps.description: For a material direct investment, the PVC principal and deal team review progress on the value creation plan (operating efficiency, digital and data projects, management changes) and agree changes with management.

next.condition: annual sustainability data cycle falls in this quarter

evidence.note: PVC supports asset management of material direct equity investments. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Consolidate the asset into the department's quarterly portfolio report
steps.description: The business management associate pulls the asset's figures, valuation change and flags into the Real Assets quarterly portfolio report and checks that every asset has reported.

evidence.note: Department-level portfolio reporting by the RA business management team is the author's assumption based on the organisation file's unit purpose.

steps.name: Review the asset at the quarterly portfolio review
steps.description: The group head and department leaders review each asset's results, valuation change, partner performance and risks, and decide to hold, put it on the watch list or prepare a disposition to recycle capital.

evidence.note: Real Estate actively assesses holdings for disposition and capital recycling (C$7.8 billion sold in F2020). Disposition share from the process map (about 3 RA dispositions a month against 83 asset-quarters); watch-list share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Agree a watch-list action plan with the partner
steps.description: The principal works with the partner or management on a recovery plan (leasing push, cost cuts, refinancing, capital deferral or a change of property manager) and reports progress to the group head.

evidence.note: Effort is the author's estimate; retail and office assets went through this path in 2020 and 2021.

steps.name: Draft the disposition proposal
steps.description: The senior associate sets out the sale options and timing, the partner's rights under the joint venture agreement (rights of first offer, tag and drag), expected proceeds against the latest valuation and use of proceeds, then files the note and sends the proposal to the disposition process.

evidence.note: Transfer and exit provisions in joint venture agreements; buy, hold and sell analysis. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: File the quarterly asset note
steps.description: The associate files the quarter's asset note (results, valuation inputs, meeting outcome, actions) and updates the asset's status in the pipeline and portfolio systems.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Partner data gaps
exceptions.description: The partner's package is incomplete or inconsistent and the associate queries the partner before the data can be re-keyed.

exceptions.name: Consent or business plan approval
exceptions.description: The partner or board brings a business plan, budget, major lease, capital project or financing for the fund's consent.

exceptions.name: Follow-on capital request
exceptions.description: New capital beyond the approved plan is needed and leaves this process as a pipeline opportunity.

exceptions.name: Watch list
exceptions.description: Results or leasing deteriorate and the principal agrees a recovery plan with the partner.

exceptions.name: Disposition
exceptions.description: The portfolio review decides to sell and a disposition proposal goes to the disposition process.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt of the quarter-end package to the quarterly asset note filed
benchmarks.population: Real estate, infrastructure and energy holdings of a large pension investor

evidence.note: Author's reading: quarterly partner or board meetings follow the package by two to four weeks, valuation inputs are needed well inside the 45-day statement deadline, and the portfolio review must finish before the next quarter's package.

benchmarks.population: Directly owned real estate under GIPS for asset owners

pain_points.description: About 60 partners report in their own formats, so figures are re-keyed into internal models and gaps are chased by email.

evidence.note: Author's judgment from the number of partners.

pain_points.description: Partner meetings and board dates are set by others and consent requests arrive with short deadlines.
Valuation inputs are needed early while partners' full quarterly reports often arrive later, so teams work from flash figures.
As a joint venture partner the fund can only steer reserved matters; day-to-day asset management sits with the partner.

sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Quarterly financial statements due to the ministers within 45 days after the quarter (s. 50(1)), which sets the valuation input deadline

assumptions: The unit is one asset-quarter. The case starts when the partner's or company's quarter-end package arrives (assumed two to three weeks after quarter end, with fuller reports later) and ends with the quarterly asset note.
Mix of asset-quarters: 62% partner-run real estate, 33% infrastructure, power and energy companies with board seats, 5% newly closed holdings. The author's split of the F2021 portfolio.

The investment team's proposal of a quarter-end value, appraiser engagement and the valuation challenge are in fin-quarterly-valuation; this workflow stops at sending inputs. That workflow expects deal team proposals about ten days after quarter end, earlier than the package timing assumed here; teams use partners' flash figures to bridge it.

Follow-on capital requests leave this workflow as a pipeline opportunity (step s16); the process map has no link from this process to screening or diligence for follow-ons, which is a gap in the organisation file.
si_specialist is an organisation role that the process map does not list for this process; it is added for the annual sustainability and climate review.

Hands-on times count focused work only; time on site visits and informal partner contact is not counted. At 83 asset-quarters a month they imply about 20 FTE and the roles state about 19 FTE, under a tenth of Real Assets' 252 staff, who also source and close deals.
The simulated median (about 26 days) matches the 25-day benchmark reading, which is itself the author's estimate; no published figure for this cycle was found.
Loaded costs per hour are the organisation file's (total compensation scaled to F2022 personnel expense, times an overhead factor of 1.25, divided by 1,950 hours).
